name: Powerbuilding

card.summary: A training style that blends powerlifting-style heavy compound lifts with bodybuilding-style volume work to build strength and muscle size together.
card.note: Heavy lifting carries the usual technique and overuse risks.

quick.overview:
Powerbuilding combines the heavy squat, bench press and deadlift focus of powerlifting with the higher-volume, muscle-targeting work of bodybuilding. The appearance payoff is muscle size and shape built on a base of strength.

One pilot study exists: an eight-week powerbuilding programme in 18 women, which measured physical activity, movement competency, strength and empowerment. Otherwise the style is discussed mainly in lifting communities.
quick.how: Programmes typically start a session with heavy, low-repetition work on a main lift and follow it with moderate-to-higher-repetition accessory exercises aimed at specific muscles. Weekly splits vary from full-body to upper/lower or push/pull/legs layouts.
quick.risks: The risks are those of resistance training in general, including technique-related strains and overuse injuries when heavy loads and high volume are combined. Beginners are generally advised by coaches to learn lifts under supervision.

lead: Powerbuilding is a hybrid approach to resistance training that merges powerlifting, in which athletes work toward a maximal total on the squat, bench press and deadlift, with bodybuilding, in which training is aimed at muscle size and symmetry.

People use it to build a more muscular physique while also getting stronger on the main lifts, so that heavy compound work provides the stimulus for mass and bodybuilding-style accessory work fills in lagging areas such as the shoulders, arms and upper back.
A 2024 pilot study, EmpowerHER, described powerbuilding as an exercise intervention that had not previously been explored and tested an eight-week programme in women [1].

chain: Heavy compound lifts drive strength and mechanical load
Higher-volume accessory work targets specific muscles
More muscle mass with a proportioned physique
angle.text: Lifters use the heavy portion to progress loads over time and the volume portion to add size where they want it. The result they describe is a physique that looks muscular and is also strong.

paras: Powerbuilding programmes pair low-repetition heavy sets on the competition lifts with accessory work in moderate and higher repetition ranges, so that the training week addresses both strength and hypertrophy. Practitioners often describe it as a middle path for people who want the look of a bodybuilder and the numbers of a powerlifter.

Because the aim includes muscle size, followers use the accessory portion to target visible areas such as shoulders, arms, chest and back, which affect the overall silhouette. Heavy lifting supports progressive overload on the large muscle groups.

A pilot study in the International Journal of Exercise Science enrolled 18 women, average age about 25, with no powerbuilding experience. They trained three times weekly for one hour over eight weeks, with physical activity and movement competency assessed before and after and three-repetition-maximum tests in the squat, bench press and deadlift in weeks one and eight [1]. The authors noted that, to their knowledge, powerbuilding had not been explored as an exercise intervention before [1].

refs.title: EmpowerHER: A Pilot Study to Increase Physical Activity and Strength Through Powerbuilding.
